references.text: The global famine (Gen 41:57) creates the necessary context for Joseph's brothers' specific journey (Gen 42:3).
Stephen confirms in the New Testament that Jacob's sending of his brothers to Egypt was the first time (Gen 42:3), placing the event within a salvation-historical context.
The general famine (Gen 41:56) is the direct cause of the brothers' journey (Gen 42:3).
Ironical parallel: The brothers sold Joseph into Egypt (Gen 37:28), and now must return there to save themselves (Gen 42:3), demonstrating God's reversal.
